description: operation_mode=ClothesDryer, confirmed. Like ComfortableDehumidification, rejects a real temperature (E-21291-01712 with temperature=20.0) and requires temperature=0.0 -- but unlike ComfortableDehumidification, no humidity field was sent here and the write still succeeded, so ClothesDryer does NOT appear to need the humidity exception.
app_confirmed: App shows clothes-drying mode active. No temperature control shown, no AI control option shown, nanoeX off.
notes: CONFIRMED: EoliaOperationMode.CLOTHES_DRYER wire value matches the app's clothes-drying mode.

Requires temperature=0.0 like ComfortableDehumidification (real value 20.0 was rejected with the same E-21291-01712 as before), but does NOT require the humidity field -- succeeded without it. So this mode is 'no temperature target' but NOT 'humidity target' -- a third category distinct from both the Cooling-family (real temp) and Dry (humidity target).

Kevin reports the app shows no AI-control option at all for this mode (not just off, but unavailable) -- consistent with a genuinely fan/utility-style mode. Untested whether ai_control being present-but-off in the payload vs. omitted matters; current payload just carries over off from cached state and it worked fine.

This mode is bucketed under HVACMode.DRY in climate.py (grouped with Dehumidifying/ComfortableDehumidification) -- still a defensible coarse-bucket choice for HA's UI even though the underlying mechanism (no temp, no humidity, just airflow) is closer to Blast's fan-only behavior than to Dry's humidity-target behavior. No code change made; flagging for awareness only.
